    • For T:X→XT : X \to XT:X→X and k≥0k \ge 0k≥0, the kkk-th Bernstein number isρk(T)=sup⁡V∈GkXg(T,V).\rho_k(T) = \sup_{V \in \mathcal{G}_k X} g(T, V).ρk​(T)=V∈Gk​Xsup​g(T,V).In particular ρ1(T)=∥T∥\rho_1(T) = \|T\|ρ1​(T)=∥T∥, and ρk(T)=0\rho_k(T) = 0ρk​(T)=0 when k>dim⁡Xk > \dim Xk>dimX.

  2. defLax606786.Cocycles

    Cocycles and their Lyapunov exponents

    A cocycle consists of an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation σ\sigmaσ of a Lebesgue probability space (Ω,μ)(\Omega, \mu)(Ω,μ) (a standard Borel space with a probability measure giving points measure zero), together with a map ω↦Lω\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\omegaω↦Lω​ from Ω\OmegaΩ into the bounded operators on a real Banach space XXX which is

    • strongly measurable: ω↦Lωx\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\omega xω↦Lω​x is measurable for each x∈Xx \in Xx∈X;
    • forward integrable: log⁡+∥Lω∥∈L1(μ)\log^+ \|\mathcal{L}_\omega\| \in L^1(\mu)log+∥Lω​∥∈L1(μ).

    No invertibility of Lω\mathcal{L}_\omegaLω​ is assumed. Its iterates are Lω(0)=id\mathcal{L}^{(0)}_\omega = \mathrm{id}Lω(0)​=id and Lω(n+1)=Lσnω∘Lω(n)\mathcal{L}^{(n+1)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}_{\sigma^n \omega} \circ \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omegaLω(n+1)​=Lσnω​∘Lω(n)​.

    All logarithms below take values in [−∞,∞)[-\infty, \infty)[−∞,∞) with log⁡0=−∞\log 0 = -\inftylog0=−∞, and indices of exponents are shifted by one from the usual convention: lambda0lambda 0lambda0 is λ1\lambda_1λ1​.

    • The growth rate of a vector is λω(x)=lim sup⁡n1nlog⁡∥Lω(n)x∥\lambda_\omega(x) = \limsup_n \frac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega x\|λω​(x)=limsupn​n1​log∥Lω(n)​x∥.
    • The kkk-th Lyapunov exponent (k≥1k \ge 1k≥1) is χk(ω)=lim sup⁡n1nlog⁡ρk(Lω(n))\chi_k(\omega) = \limsup_n \frac1n \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega)χk​(ω)=limsupn​n1​logρk​(Lω(n)​), with ρk\rho_kρk​ the Bernstein number. The sequence χ1≥χ2≥⋯\chi_1 \ge \chi_2 \ge \cdotsχ1​≥χ2​≥⋯ is non-increasing and χ1=λ1\chi_1 = \lambda_1χ1​=λ1​ is the top exponent.
    • The distinct exponents λ1>λ2>⋯\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdotsλ1​>λ2​>⋯ are the distinct values of χk\chi_kχk​: λ1=χ1\lambda_1 = \chi_1λ1​=χ1​ and λi+1=χt\lambda_{i+1} = \chi_tλi+1​=χt​ for the least ttt with χt<λi\chi_t < \lambda_iχt​<λi​. The multiplicity mim_imi​ of λi\lambda_iλi​ is the number of kkk with χk=λi\chi_k = \lambda_iχk​=λi​. When there is no exponent after λi\lambda_iλi​ the recursion stops: mim_imi​ is recorded as 000, and the later λ\lambdaλ's are −∞-\infty−∞.
    • The index of compactness is ν(ω)=lim⁡kχk(ω)=inf⁡kχk(ω)\nu(\omega) = \lim_k \chi_k(\omega) = \inf_k \chi_k(\omega)ν(ω)=limk​χk​(ω)=infk​χk​(ω).
    • The cocycle is quasicompact if ν<λ1\nu < \lambda_1ν<λ1​ almost everywhere.
    • A family of operators ω↦Pω\omega \mapsto P_\omegaω↦Pω​ is tempered if ω↦log⁡∥Pω∥\omega \mapsto \log \|P_\omega\|ω↦log∥Pω​∥ is tempered for (σ,μ)(\sigma, \mu)(σ,μ).

    49variable {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    50 [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X]
    51
    52/-- A strongly measurable, forward-integrable cocycle of bounded operators on `X` over an
    53invertible ergodic transformation of a Lebesgue probability space. -/
    54structure Cocycle (Ω X : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    55 [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X] where
    56 /-- The base transformation, a measurable bijection with measurable inverse. -/
    57 σ : Ω ≃ᵐ Ω
    58 /-- The invariant measure. -/
    59 μ : Measure Ω
    60 /-- The generator `ω ↦ 𝓛_ω`. -/
    61 L : Ω → X →L[ℝ] X
    62 isProbability : IsProbabilityMeasure μ
    63 nullSingleton : NullSingletonClass μ
    64 ergodic : Ergodic σ μ
    65 stronglyMeasurable : ∀ x : X, Measurable (fun ω => L ω x)
    66 forwardIntegrable : Integrable (fun ω => Real.log (max ‖L ω‖ 1)) μ
    67
    68attribute [instance] Cocycle.isProbability Cocycle.nullSingleton
    69
    70namespace Cocycle
    71
    72/-- `𝓛^{(n)}_ω = 𝓛_{σ^{n-1}ω} ∘ ⋯ ∘ 𝓛_ω`. -/
    73noncomputable def iterate (R : Cocycle Ω X) : ℕ → Ω → X →L[ℝ] X
    74 | 0, _ => ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ X
    75 | n + 1, ω => (R.L (R.σ^[n] ω)).comp (R.iterate n ω)
    76
    77/-- `λ_ω(x) = limsup (1/n) log ‖𝓛^{(n)}_ω x‖`. -/
    78noncomputable def lambdaAt (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) (x : X) : EReal :=
    79 limsup (fun n : ℕ => logEReal ‖R.iterate n ω x‖ / (n : EReal)) atTop
    80
    81/-- `χ_k(ω) = limsup (1/n) log ρ_k(𝓛^{(n)}_ω)`. Meaningful for `k ≥ 1`; `χ_0 = -∞`. -/
    82noncomputable def chi (R : Cocycle Ω X) (k : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : EReal :=
    83 limsup (fun n : ℕ => logEReal (bernsteinNumber (R.iterate n ω) k) / (n : EReal)) atTop
    84
    85/-- The index `k` at which the `(i+1)`-st distinct exponent first occurs among the `χ_k`:
    86`1` for `i = 0`, then the least `t ≥ 1` with `χ_t` below the previous distinct exponent,
    87and `0` once there is none. -/
    88noncomputable def lambdaIdx (R : Cocycle Ω X) : ℕ → Ω → ℕ
    89 | 0, _ => 1
    90 | (i + 1), ω => sInf {t : ℕ | 1 ≤ t ∧ R.chi t ω < R.chi (R.lambdaIdx i ω) ω}
    91
    92/-- `lambda i` is the distinct exponent `λ_{i+1}`. -/
    93noncomputable def lambda (R : Cocycle Ω X) (i : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : EReal :=
    94 R.chi (R.lambdaIdx i ω) ω
    95
    96/-- `mult i` is the multiplicity `m_{i+1}` of `λ_{i+1}`; `0` if `λ_{i+1}` is the last distinct
    97exponent. -/
    98noncomputable def mult (R : Cocycle Ω X) (i : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : ℕ :=
    99 R.lambdaIdx (i + 1) ω - R.lambdaIdx i ω
    100
    101/-- `ν(ω) = inf_{k ≥ 1} χ_k(ω)`. -/
    102noncomputable def nu (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) : EReal := ⨅ k : ℕ, R.chi (k + 1) ω
    103
    104/-- `ν < λ₁` almost everywhere. -/
    105def IsQuasicompact (R : Cocycle Ω X) : Prop :=
    106 ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.nu ω < R.chi 1 ω
    107
    108/-- `ω ↦ log ‖P_ω‖` is tempered. -/
    109abbrev IsTempered (R : Cocycle Ω X) (P : Ω → X →L[ℝ] X) : Prop :=
    110 Tempered R.σ R.μ (fun ω => Real.log ‖P ω‖)
    111
    112end Cocycle
    113

  3. thm✓Lax606786.OseledetsDecomposition

    The semi-invertible Oseledets decomposition

    Let L\mathcal{L}L be a cocycle on a separable Banach space XXX, over an invertible ergodic base (Ω,σ,μ)(\Omega, \sigma, \mu)(Ω,σ,μ). Let λ1>λ2>⋯\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdotsλ1​>λ2​>⋯ be its distinct Lyapunov exponents, mim_imi​ their multiplicities, and L∈{1,2,…,∞}L \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \infty\}L∈{1,2,…,∞} the number of distinct exponents. Then λi\lambda_iλi​ and mim_imi​ are almost everywhere constant, L≥2L \ge 2L≥2 if and only if L\mathcal{L}L is quasicompact, and there are

    • measurable families of subspaces Ei(ω)E_i(\omega)Ei​(ω) of dimension mim_imi​ (the fast spaces), for i<Li < Li<L,
    • strongly measurable, tempered families of projections Πl(ω)\Pi_{l}(\omega)Πl​(ω), for 2≤l≤L2 \le l \le L2≤l≤L, with ranges Vl(ω)V_l(\omega)Vl​(ω) (the slow spaces),

    such that for almost every ω\omegaω:

    1. LωEi(ω)=Ei(σω)\mathcal{L}_\omega E_i(\omega) = E_i(\sigma\omega)Lω​Ei​(ω)=Ei​(σω), and Ei(ω)E_i(\omega)Ei​(ω) grows at rate exactly λi\lambda_iλi​, both in norm and in slowest growth:lim⁡n1nlog⁡∥Lω(n)∣Ei(ω)∥=lim⁡n1nlog⁡g(Lω(n),Ei(ω))=λi;\lim_n \tfrac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega|_{E_i(\omega)}\| = \lim_n \tfrac1n \log g(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega, E_i(\omega)) = \lambda_i;nlim​n1​log∥Lω(n)​∣Ei​(ω)​∥=nlim​n1​logg(Lω(n)​,Ei​(ω))=λi​;
    2. X=E1(ω)⊕⋯⊕El−1(ω)⊕Vl(ω)X = E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_{l-1}(\omega) \oplus V_l(\omega)X=E1​(ω)⊕⋯⊕El−1​(ω)⊕Vl​(ω), and Πl(ω)\Pi_l(\omega)Πl​(ω) is the projection onto Vl(ω)V_l(\omega)Vl​(ω) along E1(ω)⊕⋯⊕El−1(ω)E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_{l-1}(\omega)E1​(ω)⊕⋯⊕El−1​(ω);
    3. LωVl(ω)⊆Vl(σω)\mathcal{L}_\omega V_l(\omega) \subseteq V_l(\sigma\omega)Lω​Vl​(ω)⊆Vl​(σω);
    4. Vl(ω)={x∈X:λω(x)≤λl}V_l(\omega) = \{x \in X : \lambda_\omega(x) \le \lambda_l\}Vl​(ω)={x∈X:λω​(x)≤λl​}.

    This is the semi-invertible form of Oseledets' multiplicative ergodic theorem (Oseledets 1968; Froyland, Lloyd and Quas 2013; González-Tokman and Quas 2014), for strongly measurable cocycles on separable Banach spaces as in Lee (2024). In other words, L\mathcal{L}L has an Oseledets decomposition in the sense of the definition of Oseledets decompositions, whose zero-based indexing the Lean statement follows. Measurability of EiE_iEi​ is with respect to the Borel structure of the Grassmannian; strong measurability of Πl\Pi_lΠl​ means that ω↦Πl(ω)x\omega \mapsto \Pi_l(\omega) xω↦Πl​(ω)x is measurable for each xxx.

  4. defLax606786.Grassmannian

    The Grassmannians of a Banach space

    Let XXX be a real normed space. The unit sphere of a subspace V≤XV \le XV≤X is SV={x∈V:∥x∥=1}\mathbb{S}_V = \{x \in V : \|x\| = 1\}SV​={x∈V:∥x∥=1}; it spans VVV, so it determines VVV.

    • The Grassmannian GX\mathcal{G} XGX is the set of closed subspaces V≤XV \le XV≤X admitting a bounded projection X→VX \to VX→V. It carries the distanced(V,W)=dH(SV,SW)∈[0,∞],d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W) \in [0, \infty],d(V,W)=dH​(SV​,SW​)∈[0,∞],the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres (infinite exactly when one of V,WV, WV,W is 000 and the other is not).
    • For k≥0k \ge 0k≥0, GkX\mathcal{G}_k XGk​X is the set of kkk-dimensional subspaces of XXX. For k≥1k \ge 1k≥1 the unit sphere SV\mathbb{S}_VSV​ is a nonempty compact set and GkX\mathcal{G}_k XGk​X carries the metric d(V,W)=dH(SV,SW)d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W)d(V,W)=dH​(SV​,SW​).

    Each is equipped with the Borel σ\sigmaσ-algebra of its distance.

    31/-- `𝒢X`: the closed subspaces of `X` admitting a bounded projection onto them. -/
    32def Grassmannian : Type _ :=
    33 {V : Submodule ℝ X // V.ClosedComplemented}
    34
    35variable {X}
    36
    37/-- Every subspace is spanned by its unit sphere. -/
    38theorem span_sphere_inter (V : Submodule ℝ X) :
    39 Submodule.span ℝ (Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V : Set X)) = V := by
    40 apply le_antisymm
    41 · exact Submodule.span_le.2 Set.inter_subset_right
    42 · intro x hx
    43 rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
    44 · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    45 · have hxeq : x = ‖x‖ • (‖x‖⁻¹ • x) := by
    46 rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0), one_smul]
    47 rw [hxeq]
    48 refine Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨?_, V.smul_mem _ hx⟩)
    49 rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
    50 inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]

    54/-- The unit sphere `𝕊_V = {x ∈ V : ‖x‖ = 1}`. -/

    58/-- `V ↦ 𝕊_V`, as a closed subset of `X`. -/

    62theorem toCloseds_injective : Function.Injective (toCloseds (X := X)) := by
    63 intro V W h

    80variable (X)
    81
    82/-- `𝒢_k X`: the `k`-dimensional subspaces of `X`. -/
    83def GrassmannianFin (k : ℕ) : Type _ :=
    84 {V : Submodule ℝ X // FiniteDimensional ℝ V ∧ Module.finrank ℝ V = k}
    85
    86variable {X}
    87
    88namespace GrassmannianFin
    89
    90/-- The unit sphere `𝕊_V = {x ∈ V : ‖x‖ = 1}`. -/
    91def sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : Set X :=
    92 Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V.1 : Set X)
    93
    94/-- `V` is the span of its unit sphere. -/
    95theorem span_sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) :
    96 Submodule.span ℝ V.sphere = (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) := by
    97 apply le_antisymm
    98 · exact Submodule.span_le.2 Set.inter_subset_right
    99 · intro x hx
    100 rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
    101 · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    102 · have hxeq : x = ‖x‖ • (‖x‖⁻¹ • x) := by
    103 rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0), one_smul]
    104 rw [hxeq]
    105 refine Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨?_, V.1.smul_mem _ hx⟩)
    106 rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
    107 inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]
    108
    109/-- `𝕊_V` is compact. -/
    110theorem isCompact_sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : IsCompact V.sphere := by
    111 have : FiniteDimensional ℝ (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) := V.2.1
    112 have himg : V.sphere =
    113 (Subtype.val : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) → X) '' Metric.sphere (0 : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) 1 := by
    114 ext x
    115 simp only [sphere, Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_image]
    116 constructor
    117 · rintro ⟨hx1, hxV⟩
    118 refine ⟨⟨x, hxV⟩, ?_, rfl⟩
    119 rwa [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm] at hx1 ⊢
    120 · rintro ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩
    121 rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm] at hv
    122 exact ⟨by rwa [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm], v.2⟩
    123 rw [himg]
    124 exact (_root_.isCompact_sphere (0 : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) 1).image continuous_subtype_val
    125
    126/-- `𝕊_V` is nonempty when `k ≠ 0`. -/
    127theorem nonempty_sphere {k : ℕ} [NeZero k] (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : V.sphere.Nonempty := by
    128 have hne : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) ≠ ⊥ := by
    129 intro h
    130 apply NeZero.ne k
    131 have hfr := V.2.2
    132 rw [h, finrank_bot] at hfr
    133 exact hfr.symm
    134 obtain ⟨x, hxV, hx0⟩ := Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot hne
    135 refine ⟨‖x‖⁻¹ • x, ?_, V.1.smul_mem _ hxV⟩
    136 rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
    137 inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]
    138
    139/-- `V ↦ 𝕊_V`, as a nonempty compact subset of `X`. -/
    140noncomputable def toNonemptyCompacts {k : ℕ} [NeZero k] (V : GrassmannianFin X k) :
    141 NonemptyCompacts X where
    142 carrier := V.sphere
    143 isCompact' := V.isCompact_sphere
    144 nonempty' := V.nonempty_sphere
    145
    146theorem toNonemptyCompacts_injective (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] :
    147 Function.Injective (toNonemptyCompacts (X := X) (k := k)) := by
    148 intro V W h
    149 apply Subtype.ext
    150 rw [← V.span_sphere, ← W.span_sphere]
    151 exact congrArg (fun s : NonemptyCompacts X => Submodule.span ℝ (s : Set X)) h
    152
    153/-- The metric on `𝒢_k X`: the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres. -/
    154noncomputable instance instMetricSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] : MetricSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) :=
    155 MetricSpace.induced toNonemptyCompacts (toNonemptyCompacts_injective k) inferInstance
    156
    157/-- The Borel `σ`-algebra of that metric. -/
    158noncomputable instance instMeasurableSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] :
    159 MeasurableSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) :=
    160 borel (GrassmannianFin X k)
    161
    162instance instBorelSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] : BorelSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) := ⟨rfl⟩
    163
    164end GrassmannianFin
    165
    166end Lax606786.Grassmannian

  5. defLax606786.SubadditiveFamilies

    Subadditive families of measurable functions

    Let σ:Ω→Ω\sigma : \Omega \to \Omegaσ:Ω→Ω be a map on a measurable space. A sequence (fn)n≥0(f_n)_{n \ge 0}(fn​)n≥0​ of measurable functions Ω→R\Omega \to \mathbb{R}Ω→R is a subadditive family over σ\sigmaσ if

    fm+n(ω)≤fm(σnω)+fn(ω)for all m,n≥0 and ω∈Ω.f_{m+n}(\omega) \le f_m(\sigma^n \omega) + f_n(\omega) \quad \text{for all } m, n \ge 0 \text{ and } \omega \in \Omega.fm+n​(ω)≤fm​(σnω)+fn​(ω)for all m,n≥0 and ω∈Ω.

    The typical example is fn(ω)=log⁡∥Lω(n)∥f_n(\omega) = \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|fn​(ω)=log∥Lω(n)​∥ for a cocycle L\mathcal{L}L of bounded operators.

    19/-- `(f_n)` is a subadditive family of measurable functions over `σ`. -/
    20def IsSubadditiveFamily {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (σ : Ω → Ω) (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) : Prop :=
    21 (∀ n, Measurable (f n)) ∧ ∀ m n ω, f (m + n) ω ≤ f m (σ^[n] ω) + f n ω

  6. thm✓Lax606786.KingmanTheorem

    Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem

    Let σ\sigmaσ be an ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a probability space (Ω,μ)(\Omega, \mu)(Ω,μ), and let (fn)(f_n)(fn​) be a subadditive family of integrable functions over σ\sigmaσ. Then there is a constant C∈[−∞,∞)C \in [-\infty, \infty)C∈[−∞,∞) such that

    C=lim⁡n→∞1n∫fn dμand1nfn(ω)→Cfor μ-a.e. ω.C = \lim_{n \to \infty} \tfrac1n \int f_n \, d\mu \qquad \text{and} \qquad \tfrac1n f_n(\omega) \to C \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega.C=n→∞lim​n1​∫fn​dμandn1​fn​(ω)→Cfor μ-a.e. ω.

    Limits are taken in the extended reals [−∞,∞][-\infty, \infty][−∞,∞]. The theorem is due to Kingman (1968).

    25/-- Kingman's theorem: `f_n / n` converges almost everywhere to the constant
    26`C = lim (1/n) ∫ f_n ∈ [-∞, ∞)`. -/
    27axiom kingman {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    28 (σ : Ω → Ω) (hσ : Ergodic σ μ) (f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (hf : IsSubadditiveFamily σ f)
    29 (hint : ∀ n, Integrable (f n) μ) :
    30 ∃ C : EReal, C ≠ ⊤ ∧
    31 Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (((∫ ω, f n ω ∂μ) / n : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧
    32 ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f n ω / n : EReal)) atTop (𝓝 C)
    33

  7. thm✓Lax606786.BalancedKingman

    Kingman's theorem for balanced intervals

    Let σ\sigmaσ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a Lebesgue probability space (Ω,μ)(\Omega, \mu)(Ω,μ) (a standard Borel space with a probability measure giving points measure zero), and let (fn)(f_n)(fn​) be a subadditive family of integrable functions over σ\sigmaσ. Then the averages over the balanced time intervals [−n,n)[-n, n)[−n,n) converge to the same constant as in Kingman's theorem:

    12nf2n(σ−nω)→C=lim⁡n→∞1n∫fn dμfor μ-a.e. ω,\tfrac{1}{2n} f_{2n}(\sigma^{-n}\omega) \to C = \lim_{n \to \infty} \tfrac1n \int f_n \, d\mu \quad \text{for } \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega,2n1​f2n​(σ−nω)→C=n→∞lim​n1​∫fn​dμfor μ-a.e. ω,

    with C∈[−∞,∞)C \in [-\infty, \infty)C∈[−∞,∞) and limits taken in the extended reals. This is the balanced subadditive ergodic theorem of Lee (2024).

  9. thm✓Lax606786.IndexOfCompactness

    The index of compactness is the growth rate of the compactness seminorm

    Let L\mathcal{L}L be a cocycle on a separable Banach space XXX. If the growth rate of the compactness seminorm of the iterates exists and is almost everywhere equal to a constant κ∈[−∞,∞]\kappa \in [-\infty, \infty]κ∈[−∞,∞],

    lim⁡n1nlog⁡∥Lω(n)∥c=κfor a.e. ω,\lim_n \tfrac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c = \kappa \quad \text{for a.e. } \omega,nlim​n1​log∥Lω(n)​∥c​=κfor a.e. ω,

    then the index of compactness ν=lim⁡kχk\nu = \lim_k \chi_kν=limk​χk​ equals κ\kappaκ almost everywhere. This is the equivalence of growth statistics in the appendix of Lee (2024).

  10. thm✓Lax606786.SlowSpaceNonmeasurability

    Slow spaces on a separable Banach space need not be measurable

    Let Ω={±1}Z\Omega = \{\pm1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}Ω={±1}Z with its product σ\sigmaσ-algebra, and let X=ℓ1(Z)X = \ell^1(\mathbb{Z})X=ℓ1(Z). For ω∈Ω\omega \in \Omegaω∈Ω let

    Then XXX is separable and every VωV_\omegaVω​ belongs to the Grassmannian GX\mathcal{G} XGX, but there is no measurable map W:Ω→GXW : \Omega \to \mathcal{G} XW:Ω→GX with W(ω)=VωW(\omega) = V_\omegaW(ω)=Vω​ for every ω∈Ω\omega \in \Omegaω∈Ω.

    Over the shift σ(ω)n=ωn+1\sigma(\omega)_n = \omega_{n+1}σ(ω)n​=ωn+1​ with the Bernoulli measure, the operators Lωx=φω(x) e0\mathcal{L}_\omega x = \varphi_\omega(x)\, e_0Lω​x=φω​(x)e0​ form a cocycle of rank one with λ1=0\lambda_1 = 0λ1​=0, fast space E1(ω)=span⁡{e0}E_1(\omega) = \operatorname{span}\{e_0\}E1​(ω)=span{e0​} and slow space VωV_\omegaVω​; so separability of XXX alone does not make the slow spaces measurable. This example is due to J. A. Horan (PhD thesis, University of Victoria, 2020). The argument: distinct VωV_\omegaVω​ are at distance at least 111 in GX\mathcal{G} XGX and Vω=V−ωV_\omega = V_{-\omega}Vω​=V−ω​, so a measurable WWW would make every set S=−SS = -SS=−S measurable, while there are more such sets than measurable ones.

    In Lean a sign ωi∈{±1}\omega_i \in \{\pm1\}ωi​∈{±1} is coded by a boolean, truetruetrue for +1+1+1.
